requirement: Describe the prospective single-site randomized parallel two-arm trial in adults living with HIV who smoke daily and want to quit, comparing tailored nicotine-replacement therapy with standard-care nicotine-replacement therapy.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the target population, randomized two-arm design and standard versus tailored NRT interventions.

requirement: Apply the protocol eligibility frame: age greater than 18 years, daily smoking, English or Spanish fluency, care in the partner HIV-clinic networks, interest in quitting and Readiness to Quit Ladder score greater than 6, with exclusions for competing cessation/weight-control programs and stated psychiatric or nicotine-replacement contraindications.
acceptable_values: Readiness to Quit Ladder greater than 6

evidence.text: The target-population and inclusion/exclusion section states the age, language, clinic, smoking, readiness and safety criteria.

requirement: Implement individual 1:1 allocation using statistician-generated randomly permuted blocks within prespecified strata, and identify the actual stratification factors, block sizes, concealment mechanism and masked roles before finalization; do not infer these from post-randomization balance checks.

evidence.text: The protocol states 1:1 allocation and statistician-generated permuted blocks in each stratum but lists participant characteristics only in a subsequent distribution-check sentence.

requirement: Represent the treatment contrast accurately: both arms receive a brief behavioral intervention, while standard care follows phenotype/product-guided patch dosing for up to 10 weeks and the tailored arm begins before the quit attempt, uses risk-tailored patch plus nicotine gum and may continue NRT through relapse.
acceptable_values: brief behavioral intervention in both arms

evidence.text: The intervention sections distinguish the common brief counseling, standard patch schedule, tailored algorithm, gum dosing and relapse procedures.

requirement: State the primary treatment-effect estimand, including target population, tailored-versus-standard contrast, abstinence variable, follow-up time and strategies for nonadherence, treatment discontinuation, slips, relapse, dose escalation or pharmacologic rescue and death.

evidence.text: The protocol defines abstinence outcomes and arm-specific relapse/rescue procedures but does not formalize their estimand handling.

requirement: Define smoking-cessation outcomes as 7-day and 30-day point-prevalence abstinence and verified continuous abstinence at 3, 6 and 12 months after the scheduled quit day, with quit attempts and consecutive abstinent days retained as supporting outcomes.

evidence.text: The main-outcomes section lists point-prevalence, continuous-abstinence, quit-attempt and duration outcomes at 3, 6 and 12 months.

requirement: Biochemically verify abstinence using carbon monoxide below 10 ppm and cotinine below 15 ng/mL, while classifying participants with unverifiable biological samples or loss to follow-up as non-abstinent.

evidence.text: The protocol states both biochemical thresholds and the conservative classification for unverifiable or lost participants.

requirement: Anchor outcome presentation to baseline, the one-month monitoring visit and 3-, 6- and 12-month post-quit follow-ups, and distinguish the primary six-month assessment used for power/modeling from the additional visits.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies the smoking follow-ups, one-month visit and follow-up procedures.
The power calculation is based on the six-month primary endpoint while the hypothesis also names 12 months.

requirement: Analyze the prespecified secondary clinical and patient-reported domains separately from abstinence: CD4, HIV viral load, blood pressure and pulse, body mass index, waist and hip circumference, health-related quality of life, withdrawal, craving, mood, neurocognition, BDNF and body-image measures.

evidence.text: The protocol lists secondary HIV, physiologic, anthropometric, quality-of-life, withdrawal, mood, neurocognitive, biomarker and body-image measures.

requirement: Resolve the confirmatory endpoint hierarchy before finalization: the protocol presents several abstinence definitions at 3, 6 and 12 months, whereas the reference powers 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at six months but calls abstinence at both 6 and 12 months primary.
acceptable_values: single primary variable and timepoint identified

evidence.text: The protocol names multiple abstinence definitions at 3, 6 and 12 months without a single confirmatory hierarchy.
The reference bases power on six months, labels 6- and 12-month abstinence primary and then specifies six-month 7-day point prevalence.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy population and preserve randomized-arm attribution; explicitly state whether all randomized participants remain included regardless of NRT initiation, adherence, dose changes, relapse, rescue treatment and post-baseline data availability.

evidence.text: The protocol defines allocation and arm-specific treatment adaptations but no statistical analysis population.

requirement: Compare six-month 7-day point-prevalence abstinence between tailored and standard-care arms using logistic regression and express the treatment coefficient as an odds ratio.

evidence.text: The reference specifies logistic regression and an odds-ratio treatment effect for six-month 7-day point prevalence.

requirement: Predefine the adjusted logistic-regression covariates rather than adding an open-ended set 'as deemed appropriate'; at minimum adjudicate gender, race, age, nicotine dependence, HIV disease stage and other drug use, and report both unadjusted and adjusted treatment effects if retained.

evidence.text: The logistic model lists candidate covariates but leaves the set open with 'and others, as deemed appropriate'.
The protocol says analyses will be performed with and without covariates to assess confounding.

requirement: Analyze repeated binary point-prevalence abstinence with a likelihood-based generalized linear mixed model containing treatment, time and treatment-by-time interaction; specify the link, visit coding, participant random effects, covariance, estimation, denominator degrees of freedom and planned contrasts.

evidence.text: The reference calls for SAS PROC GLIMMIX with treatment, time and interaction but does not operationalize the remaining model details.

requirement: If effect modification is retained, predefine a limited set of treatment-by-time-by-covariate interactions, their coding and inferential role; do not data-mine the open-ended examples of gender, race, age and nicotine-dependence grade.

evidence.text: The reference proposes higher-order interactions and gives gender, race, age and dependence only as examples.

requirement: For binary abstinence, retain the protocol rule that loss to follow-up or unavailable biochemical verification is classified as non-abstinence, and keep that composite-failure rule distinct from likelihood-based handling of intermittently missing repeated outcomes.

evidence.text: The protocol explicitly assigns unverifiable and lost-to-follow-up participants to non-abstinence.
The reference separately discusses likelihood-based repeated-model handling under MCAR or MAR.

requirement: Operationalize the repeated-model MAR analysis by specifying which baseline covariates and prior outcomes may enter the missingness/outcome model, how attrition associations are assessed, and how conclusions are reported if the augmented model differs from the base model.

evidence.text: The reference proposes checking attrition against covariates or prior outcomes and augmenting longitudinal models but gives no selection procedure.

requirement: Perform a prespecified MNAR sensitivity analysis using a selection model, pattern-mixture model or both, with explicit identifying restrictions, departure parameters and tipping-point or scenario grid; the reference's generic naming of model classes is not executable by itself.

evidence.text: The reference identifies selection and pattern-mixture models for MNAR sensitivity without specifying parameters or scenarios.

requirement: If mediation is analyzed, prespecify the behavioral outcome, mediator timepoints, treatment and mediator models, effect scale, direct and indirect effects, uncertainty method and temporal ordering for knowledge, smoking self-efficacy, craving, mood and BDNF.

evidence.text: The reference names candidate mediators and a coefficient-change sequence but leaves key causal and inferential details unresolved.

requirement: If principal-components adjustment is used for confounders, define the candidate variable matrix, preprocessing and scaling, component-retention criterion, placement in each outcome model and interpretation of the stated post-hoc variable examination.

evidence.text: The reference proposes principal-components modeling followed by post-hoc examination but supplies no operational selection or modeling rule.

requirement: Resolve the prospective sample-size conflict: the protocol says 500 participants will be allocated 1:1, whereas the reference plans to recruit 600 so that 500 remain after 15% attrition; preserve both source statements until adjudicated and do not substitute the registry's later actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol states that 500 HIV-positive smokers will be allocated 1:1.
The reference states recruitment of 600, 15% attrition and at least 500 or 250 per arm at study end.

requirement: Reproduce and independently verify the reference power assumptions: two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power, 10% six-month abstinence under standard care and a minimally important tailored-arm rate of at least 19%; reconcile the stated 600 recruited/500 retained calculation with the exact independent-proportions method.

evidence.text: The reference gives the alpha, power, assumed rates, G*Power program and recruitment/attrition numbers but not a fully reproducible parameterization.

requirement: Define the safety population and summarize SAFTEE adverse events by randomized arm, severity, frequency, relationship to NRT, action and discontinuation; separately summarize patch/gum exposure and adherence from direct observation, ACTG self-report and used-versus-dispensed quantities.

evidence.text: The protocol defines three adherence measures, SAFTEE categorization and tracking of patch/gum use and side effects but no statistical safety population or display conventions.

requirement: Before release, confirm from source history that the protocol and analysis document dated 2016-03-24 are an unmodified prospective governing pair: both predate the 2016-05 start, but the reference says models 'included' covariates and refers to analysis 'conducted previously'; exclude the family if those phrases reflect observed study data rather than proposal-style tense.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies NCT02982772 and is dated 2016-03-24, before the registry's 2016-05 study start.
The separate analysis document shares the title, NCT and date but contains isolated past-tense mediation and full-model wording.

requirement: Keep the three-page reference analysis document annotation-only: the model-visible protocol may provide design, interventions, outcomes, visits and broad covariate intent, but must not expose the reference-only power calculation, logistic regression, repeated-binary GLMM, MNAR sensitivity, mediation sequence or PCA plan.
acceptable_values: power and model decisions not model-visible

evidence.text: Full-page text and visual review found no copy of the reference's endpoint-specific regression, GLMM, sensitivity, mediation or PCA plan.
The independent reference contains the target statistical decisions and remains under the reference role.
